title: Seven more links added in the newer lists have no index, so removing a staff login or a gym reads those lists for every gym
what: Lists added in this stretch of changes point at a staff login, a gym or a payment record with no index on that link: personal-training bookings, browser alert sign-ups, member message threads (the chosen trainer) and message lines (the gym and the staff who wrote them), plus the plan payment links and the booked plan changes (payment record). When a staff login, a gym or a payment record is removed, the database reads the whole list across all gyms to find the matching lines. Message lines grow fastest, with every message at every gym. The database's own advisor flags all seven. Small today.
expected: Every link has an index that starts with the linked column, so a removal touches only its own rows.
how_often: each time a staff login, gym or payment record is removed
fix_line: Add one index on each of the seven links in a small additive change

title: The owner's list of direct reads of their gym goes through the whole two-year record, and the gym index made for it is never used
what: When an owner opens the record of direct reads of their gym's data, the database walks the record of every direct read for all gyms, newest first, until it finds 100 that name this gym or no gym. The search is written in a way the gym index cannot help with, so the advisor says that index has never been used. For a gym that is rarely named, each opening reads up to two years of everyone's entries.
expected: The owner's list uses the gym index and reads only the entries that name this gym, plus the few that name none.
who: gym owners checking who read their data
how_often: each time the record is opened
fix_line: Write the gym filter as an array-contains test so the gym index is used, and add the no-gym entries separately
